summary: Instagram is doing nearly all the work: most Hindi videos get 100 to 1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 30 views. The best videos use a surprising 'it can't do X, yet it does' hook (like the clap switch that only hears noise) about familiar sensors such as motion, IR and line-follower robots. Weak ones are plain 'how does X work?' titles on everyday gadgets (taps, doors, smoke alarms), which get few likes, shares or saves.
winningPattern: Hindi, Instagram-first Shorts about a simple sensor or robot behaviour that makers can build with Arduino. The title opens with a surprising or personified claim ('Clap Switch Taali Nahi, Sirf Shor Sunta Hai', 'Line Follower Robot Ke Paas Dimaag Nahi Hota', 'Motion Sensor Aapko Dekhta Nahi!'), then ends with a question or an emoji. Robot or maker projects get the shares and saves; generic public-place gadgets do not.
doMore: Open every title with a surprising contradiction: 'X can't do Y, yet it does'
Pick sensors and robots a student can build with Arduino, such as clap switch, PIR, IR and line follower
Post to Instagram first and optimise for shares and saves, since that is where the audience is
End each video with a clear takeaway or a 'save this for your project' line to raise saves
Test YouTube separately with a stronger first 2 seconds, as the same cut is not landing there
stopDoing: Stop making near-duplicate videos on the same topic (two smoke detector, two automatic tap, two IR sensor videos split the audience)
Stop plain 'X kaise kaam karta hai?' titles for everyday public gadgets like mall doors, lifts and washroom taps
Stop mixing in English videos with no Instagram version until you have tested them there
